metadata.notes: The real, distinct sibling of ROAST/BAKE, not a duplicate — same 'genuinely different named dish, not the same technique at a different setting' test onion.json's CARAMELIZE and potato.json's/garlic.json's/onion.json's own ROAST additions already applied: GRILL is real, DIRECT, open radiant/conductive heat (charcoal/gas grates, requiredTools: ['grill']), producing real char marks and smoke flavor neither an oven (BAKE/ROAST) nor a stovetop pan (FRY) can — a genuinely different real dish class ('grilled vegetables'), not roasted vegetables under a different name. requiredIngredientCapabilities: ['isFryingMedium'] mirrors ROAST's own reasoning (real technique brushes/coats with oil before grilling, both for flavor and to prevent sticking/aid char) — the same real, checkable distinction from a theoretical 'dry grilling' this repo doesn't attempt to model.
metadata.temperatureNote: 191-232°C (375-450°F) direct heat — the commonly-cited range across multiple independently-checked consumer grilling sources for both potato and onion (REFERENCES.md), overlapping ROAST's own 204-232°C band on purpose: both are real, comparably high-heat techniques, the DIRECT-vs-enclosed heat delivery is the actual distinguishing physical fact, not the temperature number itself.
metadata.durationNote: 480-1800s (8-30 minutes) — a real range reflecting genuine ingredient/prep dependency, not a single point figure: onion rounds/wedges commonly run 8-15 minutes total (both sides); potato (usually parboiled first — see alkaline_parboil.json/potato.json's own statePrerequisites, though a plain BOIL/SIMMER parboil is the more commonly-cited prerequisite for grilling specifically, not the alkaline variant) commonly runs 15-30 minutes. Same 'be flexible with measures' discipline roast.json's own durationNote already applies.
metadata.statePrerequisitesNote: Deliberately NO statePrerequisites entry on this action itself — like ROAST, real technique varies by ingredient (see each entity's own grillNote for what it specifically requires/recommends).
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true (data-level, no duplication) — re-grilling an already-finished result risks drying out/burning, the same caveat every high-heat cooking action in this vocabulary already carries.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): the paper's own 'heating' example, matching bake.json's/roast.json's identical classification — a real, elapsed-time thermal process. No place.ts/heat-source.ts wiring exists (grill.json has no thermophysical data, the same honest gap oven.json's own actionKindNote already names for its own tool) — applyAction executes it atomically today.
metadata.requiresActiveAttentionNote: Added 2026-08-17 (DAG-execution ticket, action.ts's own requiresActiveAttention doc comment) — classified ACTIVE. Direct open-flame/grate heat needs watching and flipping to avoid burning, the same profile as FRY.

verification.description: Visible char/grill marks on the surface, tender when pierced — a real, ADDITIONAL criterion (char marks) neither BAKE's nor ROAST's own verification needs

hazards.note: Open flame/hot grates — direct burn risk, plus real fire/flare-up risk from dripping oil that neither an oven nor a stovetop pan carries
